bug_semantics: The S3 attachment URL endpoint POST /api/attachments/:datasourceId/url became callable by BASIC app users while getSignedUploadURL still trusted request-body bucket and key values. It loaded the selected S3 datasource's stored IAM credentials, then signed PutObjectCommand({ Bucket: bucket, Key: key }); a BASIC user with a valid in-app datasource ID could therefore obtain a PutObject URL for an arbitrary bucket reachable by those credentials. The regression first shipped in 3.39.4. Git history shows the arbitrary-bucket path was closed in 3.39.8 by requiring the requested bucket to equal datasource.config.bucket, even though the advisory metadata conservatively names 3.40.0 as the patched version and the TABLE/WRITE route intentionally remains available to BASIC users.
flaw_origin: 23d75319026aec328a707e40e9437cb3bd6d9912 ('allow app users to generate S3 upload signed URLs', Conor Webb, 2026-05-28) is the smallest regression BIC: it directly replaced authorized(BUILDER) with authorized(PermissionType.TABLE, PermissionLevel.READ), exposing the pre-existing caller-controlled S3 Bucket signing sink to app users. Its direct parent d180697c7d5ed9c744e2508694b29c3a94c771eb still requires BUILDER. Follow-up 9d198b1b00acf8c4ef702f2ebe7758cf0485eead added the BASIC-user HTTP-200 regression test, and 3e881e13186eb9da19c37deb2f55b3ab46e560b8 changed READ to the advisory's final TABLE/WRITE spelling; neither is the first exploitable change, so 23d75319026aec328a707e40e9437cb3bd6d9912 is the true BIC rather than the later literal WRITE edit.

reasoning: The security boundary is the combination of low-privilege route reachability and the existing arbitrary-bucket signing sink. Although the published root-cause text names TABLE/WRITE, 23d75319026aec328a707e40e9437cb3bd6d9912 already admits BASIC users via TABLE/READ and therefore creates the exploit; 3e881e13186eb9da19c37deb2f55b3ab46e560b8 only tightens READ to WRITE after a BASIC-user success test was added. The direct parent has BUILDER authorization, so the regression is directly absent there. Commit 3c235f3456dcfcaf58675f86249060731beec346 closes cross-bucket signing by binding the request bucket to the datasource bucket; its retained BASIC-user success test explains why the route remains TABLE/WRITE. Git tags prove this code fix first appears in 3.39.8, earlier than the advisory's stated 3.40.0 patched boundary. AI attribution is judged only on the true BIC commit object: it is a normal human-authored commit with no AI marker, so the closed verdict is NOT_AI; branch names and any AI signal on later fix work are intentionally ignored.
